title: The project remote is bound by the first publish and reused: repository.publish accepts null, refuses unbound, serves the remote read
description:

The wrapper's publisher pushes `request.remoteUrl` from the publish ledger (orchestrator/node-publisher.ts:41-47; repository/publish-ledger.ts:20-27 PublishRequest, :76+ readPublishLedger decodes the decision result) and the runs read carries `remoteUrl` (http/runs-read-contract.ts:97) - keeping the RESULT shape means publisher, receipt and runs read stay untouched.
- A new command kind costs the PR #21 roster backfill (vocabulary + families + registry + v2 registry + MCP exclusion + bootstrap-sequence + 7 pinned tests + contracts runtime-vocabulary + generated client + 4 digest mirrors, memory prs19-22-landed-2026-09-03) - about 20 files; REJECTED at plan time. `project.admin` is only a capability name (daemon-command-vocabulary.ts:66) and the project configuration manifest is the provider profile (packages/contracts/src/configuration/project-configuration-contract.ts:164-169) - neither is a settings writer.
- Read routes: registered in apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener-read-dispatch.ts (pattern: sessions-read.ts + SESSIONS_READ_PATH at :32/:86/:431/:481) with the control-room pins apps/control-room/src/live/dev-proxy-paths.ts:36 and live/live-document-proxy.test.ts:34; a new read = the 8-touchpoint + `.js` bridge pattern (memory ui-connect-everything-built-2026-09-02).

FEATURE: (1) `repository.publish {goalId, remoteUrl}` keeps its exact key roster; `remoteUrl` is a string OR null. A string: admitted as today (invalid -> the existing BOOTSTRAP_PAYLOAD_INVALID, or a distinct REMOTE_URL_INVALID only if BOOTSTRAP_REFUSAL_CODES' pins are <= 2 files - architect measures and states), then ONE multi-leg decision (`commitAcceptedLegs`, bootstrap-ledger.ts:222-240): the publish request on `publish:<goalId>` exactly as today AND `RepositoryRemoteBound {remoteUrl, boundAt, boundBy}` on the project aggregate `remote:<projectId>` (replacing any prior binding; version-fenced). Null: read the bound remote; none -> PUBLISH_REMOTE_UNBOUND (DAEMON_PREREQUISITE); else commit the publish request with the RESOLVED remoteUrl in the result (publisher/receipt/runs unchanged). (2) `readProjectRemote(store, projectId)` in repository/publish-ledger.ts (or a sibling module if the file would pass 250) folding the latest RepositoryRemoteBound. (3) Read route `POST /repository/remote/read {}` -> `{ outcome: "REMOTE", remoteUrl: string|null, boundAt: string|null, boundBy: string|null }` under the GOAL capability (same as /goals/source/read), with the 8 touchpoints: route module (+ .js bridge), dispatch registration, read contract, control-room live decoder (exact keys) + dev-proxy-paths pin + live-document-proxy.test pin, daemon-store-dependencies snapshot if it enumerates read ports.
definitionOfDone: Over a REAL store: `repository.publish` with a valid URL commits the publish request (result {goalId, remoteUrl, requestedAt} byte-identical to today's shape) AND `remote:<projectId>` reads {remoteUrl, boundAt, boundBy}; a second publish with `remoteUrl: null` resolves the bound URL into its result; a publish with a DIFFERENT URL rebinds (the read returns the new one) - all asserted by reading the store.

Refusals with code + layer: `remoteUrl: null` with nothing bound -> PUBLISH_REMOTE_UNBOUND / DAEMON_PREREQUISITE; an invalid URL (embedded credential, non-https/ssh) -> the code the plan names (existing BOOTSTRAP_PAYLOAD_INVALID or REMOTE_URL_INVALID with its pins updated); a missing `remoteUrl` KEY still refuses at the payload roster (exact keys unchanged - assert the code); each arm verified red by mutation.

The wrapper publisher and runs read are untouched: `git diff --stat` shows no change under apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/ or apps/daemon/src/http/runs-read*.ts; node-publisher.test.ts and runs-read tests green unchanged (count lines quoted).

`POST /repository/remote/read {}` answers {outcome:"REMOTE", remoteUrl, boundAt, boundBy} (nulls when unbound) with its exact-key control-room decoder and the two proxy-path pins updated; the served-read roster test (if one enumerates routes) updated; MCP allowlist unchanged (the read is operator HTTP only) - count line quoted.

FAIL-CLOSED RULING made explicit in the test (step text was ambiguous): when the LATEST RepositoryRemoteBound event is unreadable or its URL no longer admits, `readProjectRemote` answers NULL rather than falling back to the binding it replaced. Falling back would push a goal to a SUPERSEDED remote, which is the defect this read exists to prevent. Arm: "refuses to fall back to an older binding when the LATEST one is unreadable" - asserts the good binding reads first, then reads null after a broken one lands.

MEASURED FOR STEP 3 (corrects the step-3 text, which the step itself told me to verify):
- `ExpectedVersionDecisionLeg` (packages/store/src/decision-legs-contracts.ts:16) is `{ aggregateId, events: readonly EventDraft[], expectedVersion }`. It has NO `eventPayload`/`eventType` fields - those belong to daemon `CommitPlan` (bootstrap-ledger.ts:156). The extra leg must therefore carry `events: [{ eventId, eventType, payload: Uint8Array }]`.
- `versionOf(ledger, remoteAggregateId(projectId))` WOULD ALWAYS RETURN 0: `readDurableLedger` (bootstrap-ledger.ts:96-117) keys aggregates by `decision.targetAggregateId` ONLY, and the remote leg is legs[1] whose target is `publish:<goalId>`. Using it would fence the SECOND bind at version 0 against a real version 1 and fail every rebind. The leg fence must come from `store.getAggregateVersion(remoteAggregateId(projectId))`.
- `checkPayload` (http/http-command-ingress.ts:118-126) refuses only UNEXPECTED keys, never a MISSING one, so a missing `remoteUrl` reaches the handler as `undefined` and must be refused there - the "refuses a MISSING remoteUrl key rather than reading it as null" arm exists because `undefined == null` is true in JS and a loose check would publish to the bound remote on a malformed request.

The goal/lifecycle/expectedVersion checks and the result object `{goalId, remoteUrl, requestedAt}` are carried over unchanged.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE STEP TEXT, both measured in step 1 and both load-bearing:
(1) The extra leg is `ExpectedVersionDecisionLeg` (packages/store/src/decision-legs-contracts.ts:16) = `{aggregateId, events: readonly EventDraft[], expectedVersion}`. The step's `{aggregateId, eventPayload, eventType, expectedVersion}` would not compile (and, per the step's own warning, a differently-named leg field is a silent no-op). `bindingLeg` builds `events: [{eventId: `${commandId}-RepositoryRemoteBound`, eventType, payload}]` with the payload encoded exactly like bootstrap-ledger's own `eventDraft`.
(2) The leg's fence is `store.getAggregateVersion(remoteAggregateId(projectId))`, NOT `versionOf(ledger, ...)`. `readDurableLedger` (bootstrap-ledger.ts:96-117) keys aggregates by `decision.targetAggregateId`; the remote leg is legs[1] and is NEVER a decision target, so `versionOf` would report 0 for an already-written remote aggregate and every rebind after the first would refuse EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT. The rebind arm is what proves this (it fails with the step's literal code). A comment in publish-services.ts records the reason so the next reader does not "simplify" it back.

ORDERING: the remote is resolved BEFORE the goal/lifecycle checks, matching the step text. Consequence, asserted: a publish naming an absent goal with a VALID url refuses BOOTSTRAP_PREREQUISITE_MISSING with zero events on `remote:<projectId>` - resolution reads, it never writes, so nothing is bound for a publish that never happened.

Publisher / receipt / runs read: NOT touched (result shape frozen; DoD 3 diff proof in step 4).

implementationPlan.description: ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW + COMPLETE.
